Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray reveals radiolucent streaks of air outlining the mediastinal structures (pneumomediastinum), which, combined with the history of an alcoholic binge (suggesting vomiting/retching) and neck swelling, supports a diagnosis involving alveolar rupture or esophageal injury leading to mediastinal air. Among the choices, identifying pneumomediastinum is the most accurate radiographic observation.
